findings.summary: The `completed` half of the credit guard was killed by an existing assertion BEFORE this commit and is killed by NOTHING after it -- measured both ways, and the situation it guards happens 124 times in today's 1,000-seed sweep
findings.detail: Surviving mutation: `if (completed && faulty.calls("putIfMatch") > writesBefore)` -> `if (faulty.calls("putIfMatch") > writesBefore)`. MEASURED on the staged tree: full `:sequencer:test` BUILD SUCCESSFUL (1m 1s, every class, sweep included), and the sweep itself green at 1,732 graceful releases against 1,608 unmutated. MEASURED on HEAD (all five sequencer test files restored from HEAD, same one-line mutation against the old `faulty.calls() > callsBefore` form): `GracefulReleaseMeterTest > aRefusalBLAMINGANOTHERPODIsCountedAndTheReleaseIsNotCredited` FAILED. The mechanism is exactly the premise change: `refuseIfPartitioned` used to do `calls++` BEFORE its `isPartitioned()` check, so a refused `stat` raised the old counter and `completed` was the ONLY thing keeping `released()` at 0 in that case (GracefulReleaseMeterTest.java:77-79). With the meter now watching `putIfMatch`, a refused `stat` moves no counter, so that assertion passes whether `completed` is consulted or not. Nothing else in the tree builds a window that calls `putIfMatch` SUCCESSFULLY and then throws -- but the sweep does: the 1,732 - 1,608 = 124 window delta is exactly the injected-ambiguous `putIfMatch` (`record` runs at the top, the write lands, the call throws), so an over-crediting meter is live at ~7% today and invisible because every `gracefulReleases` assertion is a floor. The meter's own javadoc still says 'Releases that RETURNED and wrote the lease back' (GracefulReleaseMeter.java:101) and `aReleaseThatNEVERREACHESTheStoreIsNotCredited` pins only the other half. Kill: a T1 case whose lambda does a successful `putIfMatch` and then throws an IOException -- `TWORefusalsInOneWindowAreCountedTWICE` already shows the throw-inside-the-lambda shape -- asserting `released()` is 0. This is the rules 4-5 inversion in substance rather than in text: no assertion string got looser, so `check-test-integrity.sh` cannot see it, and a previously-killed mutation is now free.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone edits LeaseManager.releaseLocked (or the store's ambiguous-put injection) so the lease write lands and the call then throws -- or simply deletes `completed &&` from the meter. The meter credits that window as a graceful release, the sweep's floor only rises, and the whole suite stays green while `gracefulReleases` no longer means 'the release returned'. MEASURED: 1,732 against 1,608, i.e. 124 such windows already exist per 1,000 seeds, and on HEAD the same mutation was caught by GracefulReleaseMeterTest.

findings.summary: `record("presign")` is constrained by nothing -- the third verb the done-cell names is the one verb it does not test
findings.detail: Surviving mutation: delete `record("presign");` from `presign`. MEASURED: full `:sequencer:test` ran with zero test failures (only the task-level results-file error caused by a concurrent build on this machine; no `... FAILED` line from any test). `theVerbsThatSKIPThePartitionCheckAreStillCOUNTED` (FaultInjectingStoreTest.java:104) asserts `capabilities` and `close` and stops there, while the row's own argument -- and the `record` javadoc at FaultInjectingStore.java:170 -- is that presign is the verb that arrived unnoticed and made the previous exception list stale. One more line in the same case (`faulty.presign("ctl/lease", java.time.Duration.ofMinutes(1)); assertThat(faulty.calls("presign")).isEqualTo(1);`) closes it. Not load-bearing today -- no meter or floor reads `calls("presign")` -- which is why this is minor and not major.
findings.failure_scenario: A future verb, or an edit to `presign`, drops its `record(...)` and the ledger silently under-counts that verb; a later floor built on `calls("presign")` -- the same way M5.26 built one on `calls()` -- then rests on a counter nothing pins, which is exactly the staleness this row exists to end. MEASURED: deleting `record("presign")` leaves the whole sequencer suite green.

findings.summary: The `list` half of the fix -- counted even when its injected `unreachable` fires first -- is unconstrained; moving `record("list")` back below the throw restores the old blindness, green
findings.detail: Surviving mutation: move `record("list");` from the top of `list` to just after the injected-`unreachable` throw, which is verbatim the pre-M5.29 behaviour the done-cell says it closed ('`list` was also uncounted on the ~3% of calls where its injected `unreachable` fires first, and now is'). MEASURED: full `:sequencer:test` BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 1m 1s. The killing case is one line away and the fixture is already built: `aNONPARTITIONFaultInTheWindowIsNotCountedAsARefusal` (GracefulReleaseMeterTest.java:119-135) runs `list` with `unreachable` at probability 1 and asserts the injected kinds; adding `assertThat(faulty.calls("list")).isEqualTo(1)` there reds the mutation exactly. Minor for the same reason as the presign finding: nothing reads `calls("list")` today.
findings.failure_scenario: The `record("list")` call drifts back below the injected-`unreachable` throw (a plausible edit, since every other fault check sits above the delegate call) and `list` is again uncounted on the ~3% of calls where the fault fires, with nothing red -- the exact blindness the done-cell claims to have closed. MEASURED: full `:sequencer:test` BUILD SUCCESSFUL with the call moved.
